claims.assumptions: 'operational' means the only in-tree consumer that emits actions, FailsafePolicy, which is advisory
claims.claim: A and D are the SAME state variable in this implementation. fresh[] is computed once in OnlineTrustLayer._tick and feeds both every relation/physics gate (D), the Beta update (D), and FailsafePolicy._conditions (A).
claims.evidence: source, 16 gates resolved and re-verified; 3 coupled
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: assurance architectures couple these in general
claims.next_experiment: none; this is settled by source
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: in this implementation the operational and diagnostic gates are one value

claims.claim: The hypothesis is NOT refuted at source level: no existing mechanism represents A and D independently. Quality.admissible is scoped to evidence by its own docstring, and csia_may_use is a second gate whose two halves are both about evidence.

temp_<sensor> features are already ungated by freshness (gate hard-coded 1.0) and keep contributing a RETAINED score after A closes. D != A already exists for one feature family, by omission rather than by design.
claims.next_experiment: measure whether temp_gps materially changes any diagnosis; not done here
claims.note: this is the retained-state hazard from the previous work package appearing on the evidence path; it is NOT prior art for a deliberate split

claims.claim: The motivating S0/S1 tradeoff reproduces EXACTLY through an independently written tick loop: 12/12 checks bit-for-bit against the committed invalidity-masking artifact.
Delta_ab(t) sums only over LOW(a) symmetric-difference LOW(b); if D_j = 0 for every j in that set, the tick carries no information distinguishing a from b.

A fault is self-masking under coupling iff the discriminating feature set is contained in the set of relations the fault gates off. gps_fault vs nominal satisfies this by construction, because CAUSES['gps_fault'] is the singleton ['phys_gps'] whose gate carries fresh['gps'].

The split restores identifiability during a fault IF AND ONLY IF some observable outside the coupled gate discriminates the pair. Necessity implies the split provably cannot help when the fault removes the SOURCE rather than the value.
claims.reading: identical operational state, opposite diagnosis; the prediction holds
claims.status: PROVED - NOVELTY NOT ESTABLISHED; corollary EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED (N = 1 fixture pair)

claims.claim: Under a sustained fault with D = 0, the posterior returns to EXACTLY the prior: log P(a)/P(b) -> log(pi_a/pi_b) with no evidence term at all.
claims.reading: the closed form predicts the full eight-cause implementation to 1e-5
claims.status: PROVED - NOVELTY NOT ESTABLISHED; NUMERICALLY VALIDATED

claims.claim: A coupled architecture forgets a saturated fault in n = log(threshold/Delta_0)/log(1-alpha) = 7.29 ticks, about 0.29 s at 25 Hz.
claims.note: the reversal TIME was not measured against the replay; only the steady states were. Recorded as an unvalidated consequence of validated premises.

claims.hypothesis: S1 and S2 represent explicit raw invalidity more faithfully at the operational-admissibility boundary than S0.
claims.reading: O improves from 0.000 to 0.996. But the FailsafePolicy outcome is bit-identical across all ten arms -- same transition time, same level histogram, same nav_degraded ticks. Only the reason string differs ('GPS trust 0.42' under S0, 'GPS data invalid' otherwise). On this recording, correcting the operational gate changed nothing an operator would see.
claims.status: EMPIRICAL ONLY - SUPPORTED at the gate, NULL at the recommendation
claims.why_this_matters: it undercuts the premise that the O axis is worth improving, and is the single strongest argument against the strong verdict

claims.hypothesis: S2 preserves more fault-relevant diagnostic evidence than S1 during explicit invalidity.
claims.reading: the effect is real in both regimes but comes from different terms: h_acc on the intermittent recording, status under sustained invalidity
claims.status: EMPIRICAL ONLY - SUPPORTED, but CONDITIONAL on sustained closure

claims.caveat: Pareto dominance on axes where one axis (O) has no demonstrated operational consequence is dominance on an assumption. Reported as measured; not read as vindication.
claims.hypothesis: Two-objective tradeoff: S0 low-O/high-D, S1 high-O/low-D, S2 high-O/high-D.
claims.pareto_classification_S2c: PARETO_DOMINANT over both S0 and S1
claims.status: EMPIRICAL ONLY - the PATTERN reproduces, the INTERPRETATION does not survive H1

claims.design: each split arm has a matched coupled control carrying identical evidence terms and differing in one boolean: S2a/S1Da, S2b/S1Db, S2c/S1D
claims.hypothesis: DETECTOR DOMINANCE: the improvement comes from adding an evidence term, not from decoupling D from A.
claims.reading: On M1 the h_acc term alone, WITH D coupled to A, recovers +0.138 and the split adds only +0.002 on top: detector-dominant. On every synthetic pattern the detector gain is exactly 0.0000 and the split gain is the whole effect. The difference is how long A stays closed at a stretch.
claims.resolution: the split earns its complexity in proportion to SUSTAINED closure duration, not to closed fraction
claims.status: EMPIRICAL ONLY - TRUE on the real recording, FALSE under sustained invalidity

claims.caveat: four points, one fixture family. PROVISIONAL, not a fitted relationship, and no functional form is claimed.
claims.claim: The value of the split is governed by the longest CONSECUTIVE A-closed run, not by the fraction of time A is closed.
claims.mechanism: T5: the frozen diagnosis smoother is a ~15-tick EWMA, so evidence that alternates faster than that averages away
claims.next_experiment: sweep sustained-closure duration finely and test the T5 time constant directly
claims.reading: P2 has A closed half the time and gains nothing; P1_BURST_ABOVE_TAU has A closed 3% of the time and gains something. Closed fraction is not the predictor.

claims.claim: The binary status encoding is HARMFUL under intermittent invalidity.
claims.implication: S2c is WORSE than S2b on M1 (0.966 vs 0.977) because the status term drags it down. The best arm on the real recording is the one WITHOUT the status feature.
claims.reading: c_status = 1 on a valid observation is MAXIMALLY consistent, which is strong evidence for causes that do not contain the feature -- i.e. for nominal. With 71% of M1 observations valid, the status term spends most ticks arguing against the fault. It is decisive under sustained invalidity and actively destructive under intermittent invalidity.

claims.cause: the sidecar held 'the last thing I saw' rather than being time-indexed. The core emits the tick at time tau only once a LATER sample arrives, so the sidecar answered a query for tau with state from after tau, and the coupled arm saw evidence at ticks where A was actually closed.
claims.claim: The first detector-dominance reading in this study was wrong, because of an instrument bug in this study's own sidecar.
claims.fix: an ordered log with as-of lookup; no constant changed
claims.how_it_was_caught: the automatic counterexample search reported that the words 'IV' and 'VV' produced identical downstream traces, which cannot be true if the status feature works
claims.was: S1D-S1 = +0.126, S2c-S1D = +0.002, read as detector-dominant on M1

claims.claim: This study's first h_acc freshness rule reproduced the very retained-state defect the previous work package documented.
claims.detail: gating h_acc evidence on ANY message arrival meant a healthy pre-onset accuracy kept being served as current while every arriving message carried h_acc = 0. Under P5_PERMANENT this made S2c report nominal (0.0 top share) while S2a reported gps_fault (0.961).
claims.fix: arms S2b2/S2c2 gate on the last message carrying a USABLE h_acc. Labelled POST_HOC everywhere; found by looking at a result.
claims.impact_on_the_real_recording: none. S2b2 == S2b and S2c2 == S2c to six decimals on M1, because messages with usable h_acc keep arriving during the valid gaps. The post-hoc fix cannot be accused of rescuing the M1 result because it does not change it.
claims.status: EMPIRICAL ONLY - NEGATIVE RESULT, KEPT, with a POST-HOC fix

claims.caveat: S2b's 4/4 is an artefact of the N3 bug: it distinguishes SENSOR_INVALID from TRANSPORT_MISSING only because invalid messages keep the stale h_acc alive. S2c2 achieves 4/4 without relying on that.
claims.claim: Four upstream conditions, one downstream vocabulary: S0 and S1 alias two pairs; the split arms with an h_acc term alias none.
The same raw condition means different things depending on which committed ingest path decodes it.
claims.detail: the v1.1 aircraft adapter never marks the GPS slot invalid; csia/runtime/plugins.py does, for the same fix_type < 3, into the same frozen core. A single no-fix message is enough to separate them.
claims.note: tick-count differences (106/120 words) also move with the stamping convention and are NOT counted as semantic divergence

claims.claim: Automatic search finds the semantic-collapse witness without being told what to look for, and the minimum distinguishing word length rises across the arms.
claims.reading: S0's witness has length 1: one message reporting no fix is downstream-identical to no message at all

claims.claim: GNSS is the ONLY sensor family in this stack with all four ingredients the split needs.
claims.detail: battery's only blocker is that the -1 sentinel reject does not delete the retained value; every other family has no explicit INVALID state at all
claims.implication: Reviewer G is conceded. This result is GNSS-specific in this implementation, and the audit says exactly why.
claims.status: PROVED - NOVELTY NOT ESTABLISHED (source audit only)

claims.claim: Clean controls: no arm leads with gps_fault on either clean fixture. The added-feature arms drive the clean posterior slightly LOWER (0.0 vs 6.4e-05).
claims.note: the arms are therefore NOT identical on clean data. A healthy h_acc is maximally consistent, which actively pushes gps_fault down. Directionally safe -- fewer false alarms -- but it is a change, and both clean fixtures are short and one holds the GNSS payload constant. Real-flight false-alarm behaviour is untested (see the HIL plan, LEVEL 3).

claims.caveat: wall time includes MAVLink decoding and the whole adapter path, so these are an upper bound on the arm's own cost rather than a measurement of it
claims.claim: The split has no measurable compute cost in this implementation.
NOVELTY
claims.note: No literature search was performed. Separating validity from status metadata is long-standing practice in avionics and in real-time middleware; Reviewer B is conceded. What this package establishes is a measured instance in one implemented architecture, with a closed-form model validated to 1e-5, not that any of it is new.

explicitly_not_claimed: that A and D need to be separate variables in assurance architectures generally
that the split is safe: it was tested for false alarms on two short clean fixtures only
that the status encoding used here is a good one -- it is the strongest the frozen consistency domain permits and it is harmful under intermittent invalidity (N1)
that any of this generalises beyond GNSS: the cross-sensor audit finds no other 4/4 candidate (C8)
that anything here is a hardware result -- no hardware was connected
that S2 should be adopted; no repair is proposed and the coupled alternative wins on the one real recording once the h_acc term is present
global_caveats: EXPLORATORY. S2 was designed after seeing the S0/S1 outcome. Nothing here is confirmatory (item 39).
One real recording, N = 1. Every number tagged M1_JAM is a property of that realisation, not an estimate over runs. No interval and no p-value appears anywhere in this package.
The frozen production core is unmodified; the only research object is a wrapper on layer.diag and an adapter subclass.
NOVELTY: NOT ESTABLISHED. No literature search was performed.
